nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a Rabin automaton and let $s$ be an infinite sequence of states. Then $s$ satisfies the Rabin condition of $r$, that is, for some Rabin pair $(E, F)$ of $r$ the sequence $s$ visits $E$ infinitely often and $F$ only finitely often, if and only if $s$ fails the Streett condition with the same pairs, that is, it is not the case that for every Rabin pair $(E, F)$ of $r$, if $s$ visits $E$ infinitely often…
nodes.title: Run-wise Rabin/Streett duality

nodes.summary: If the state space is finite, then a Streett automaton $r$ accepts the same language as its Muller presentation: the Muller automaton with the same transitions and initial states as $r$ whose acceptance sets are the sets $S$ of states such that, for every Streett pair $(E, F)$ of $r$, if $S$ meets $E$ then $S$ meets $F$.
nodes.title: Streett-to-Muller conversion preserves the language

nodes.summary: If the state space is finite, then a parity automaton accepts the same language as its Muller presentation, the Muller automaton obtained by converting it to its Rabin presentation and that to a Muller automaton.
nodes.title: Parity-to-Muller conversion preserves the language

nodes.summary: If the state space is finite, then a Rabin automaton $r$ accepts the same language as its Muller presentation: the Muller automaton with the same transitions and initial states as $r$ whose acceptance sets are the sets $S$ of states such that, for some Rabin pair $(E, F)$ of $r$, $S$ meets $E$ and is disjoint from $F$.
nodes.title: Rabin-to-Muller conversion preserves the language

nodes.summary: If the state space is finite, then a parity automaton $a$ accepts the same language as its Rabin presentation: the Rabin automaton with the same transitions and initial states as $a$ whose Rabin pairs are the pairs $(E_i, F_i)$ for $i \in \mathbb{N}$, where $E_i$ is the set of states of priority $2i$ and $F_i$ the set of states of priority greater than $2i$.
nodes.title: Parity-to-Rabin conversion preserves the language

nodes.summary: If the state space is finite, then a parity automaton $a$ accepts the same language as its Streett presentation: the Streett automaton with the same transitions and initial states as $a$ whose Streett pairs are the pairs $(E_i, F_i)$ for $i \in \mathbb{N}$, where $E_i$ is the set of states of priority $2i + 1$ and $F_i$ the set of states of priority greater than $2i + 1$.
nodes.title: Parity-to-Streett conversion preserves the language

nodes.summary: An infinite word $x$ is accepted by a Streett automaton $r$ if and only if there is a run $s$ of $r$ on $x$ such that for every Streett pair $(E, F)$ of $r$, if $s$ visits $E$ infinitely often then $s$ visits $F$ infinitely often.
nodes.title: Membership in the language of a Streett automaton

nodes.summary: An infinite word $x$ is accepted by a Rabin automaton $r$ if and only if there is a run $s$ of $r$ on $x$ and a Rabin pair $(E, F)$ of $r$ such that $s$ visits $E$ infinitely often and visits $F$ only finitely often.
nodes.title: Membership in the language of a Rabin automaton

nodes.summary: A Rabin automaton is a nondeterministic automaton together with a set of Rabin pairs $(E, F)$, each a pair of sets of states. A run is accepting when some pair is hit: the run visits $E$ infinitely often and $F$ only finitely often.
nodes.title: Rabin automaton

nodes.summary: A Streett automaton is a nondeterministic automaton together with a set of Streett pairs $(E, F)$, each a pair of sets of states. A run is accepting when every pair is respected: if the run visits $E$ infinitely often then it also visits $F$ infinitely often.
nodes.title: Streett automaton

nodes.summary: Given a Streett automaton with set of Streett pairs $\mathcal{P}$, this is the Muller automaton with the same states, initial states and transitions whose accepting family consists of the sets $S$ of states such that every pair $(E, F) \in \mathcal{P}$ with $S \cap E \neq \emptyset$ also satisfies $S \cap F \neq \emptyset$. A Muller automaton accepts a run when the set of states that the run visits infinitely often…
nodes.title: Muller presentation of a Streett automaton

nodes.summary: The Muller automaton of a parity automaton is the Muller presentation of its Rabin presentation. It has the same states, initial states and transitions, and its accepting family consists of the sets $S$ of states for which there is a natural number $i$ such that $S$ contains a state of priority $2i$ and no state of priority greater than $2i$. A Muller automaton accepts a run when the set of states that the run…
nodes.title: Muller presentation of a parity automaton

nodes.summary: Given a Rabin automaton with set of Rabin pairs $\mathcal{R}$, this is the Muller automaton with the same states, initial states and transitions whose accepting family consists of the sets $S$ of states for which some pair $(E, F) \in \mathcal{R}$ satisfies $S \cap E \neq \emptyset$ and $S \cap F = \emptyset$. A Muller automaton accepts a run when the set of states that the run visits infinitely often belongs to…
nodes.title: Muller presentation of a Rabin automaton

nodes.summary: Given a parity automaton with priority function $\Omega$ from states to natural numbers, this is the Rabin automaton with the same states, initial states and transitions whose Rabin pairs are the pairs $(E_i, F_i)$ for $i \in \mathbb{N}$, where $E_i = \{s : \Omega(s) = 2i\}$ and $F_i = \{s : \Omega(s) > 2i\}$.
nodes.title: Rabin presentation of a parity automaton

nodes.summary: Given a Rabin automaton, this is the Streett automaton with the same states, initial states and transitions and the same set of pairs.
nodes.title: Streett automaton with the pairs of a Rabin automaton

nodes.summary: Given a parity automaton with priority function $\Omega$ from states to natural numbers, this is the Streett automaton with the same states, initial states and transitions whose Streett pairs are the pairs $(E_i, F_i)$ for $i \in \mathbb{N}$, where $E_i = \{s : \Omega(s) = 2i + 1\}$ and $F_i = \{s : \Omega(s) > 2i + 1\}$.
nodes.title: Streett presentation of a parity automaton

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
